subject: Clarify cross-border processing & in-region data handling
messages:
From: Dana Liu <security@acme-corp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 12:12:00 +0100
Subject: Data residency & cross-border processing questions (Acme account)

Hi Jonas,

We're reviewing Redwood for production use at Acme and need a few clarifications around data residency and any cross-border processing that might happen under the standard hosted setup. Our legal and security teams raised these specific questions — could you confirm?

1) Can Redwood guarantee that customer content and generated outputs for an account pinned to EU will always be processed and stored only in EU regions (including backups and snapshots)?
2) Are there any control-plane or metadata copies (logs, billing records, audit entries, K/V caches) that are routed or stored outside the EU by default? If yes, where and under what conditions?
3) Which subprocessors have access to customer data or metadata for EU accounts? Any cross-region subprocessors we should be aware of?
4) If we require contractual language that explicitly prohibits cross-border backups and restricts subprocessors to EU-only, do you support an amended DPA or a Private deployment option?

We attached our high-level security questionnaire (Acme_SSCQ.pdf). If easier, we'd be happy to jump on a 30-min call.

Thanks,
Dana Liu
Head of Security Operations
Acme Corporation

Attachment: Acme_SSCQ.pdf
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Dana Liu <security@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 15:03:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Data residency & cross-border processing questions (Acme account)

Thanks for the clear list, Dana — appreciate the detail. Looping in Neha (privacy/compliance) and Marissa (your AE) so we can give a definitive answer and next steps.

Quick summary while we draft a fuller response:
- We support account-level region pinning (EU) for hosted customers; inference, KV cache and primary storage are provisioned in-region.
- There are some control-plane services (billing, aggregated telemetry) that live in our control plane; Neha will clarify whether that includes any customer-identifiable logs and where those are located by default.
- We can provide our standard EU DPA excerpt and a subprocessors list — attaching the excerpt now.
- If Acme requires contractual guarantees beyond our standard terms (e.g., explicit prohibition of cross-border backups), we typically handle via an amendment to the DPA or a Private deployment (VPC/on-prem). We'll propose options after Neha's details.

Proposed next steps:
1) Neha to confirm control-plane behavior and subprocessors.
2) If needed, we'll draft a DPA amendment for legal review.
3) Optional technical sync to go into architecture (Marissa to coordinate).

Best,
Jonas
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_dpa_eu_excerpt.pdf

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Data residency & cross-border processing questions (Acme account)

Hi Dana — thanks for sending the SSCQ. I went through your list and wanted to be explicit about what Redwood's hosted EU offering includes and where we draw boundaries. I'll keep this high level and flag options where contractual controls are typical.

1) Processing & primary storage:
- For an account pinned to the EU region, all inference requests, model KV cache, and primary object storage for customer content are provisioned and processed in EU region resources (we run in eu-west-1 / eu-central-1 depending on the customer's preference).
- Snapshots/backups of customer-managed datasets are, by default, stored in-region. We do not replicate backups to other regions unless replication is enabled by the customer or for disaster recovery under an approved DR plan.

2) Control-plane, telemetry & metadata:
- Our control plane (account control, billing aggregation, and certain operational telemetry) is hosted in the US. The control plane receives metadata required for routing and billing (e.g., account ids, project names, high-level usage metrics).
- We treat control-plane logs as operational metadata; they do not contain full customer prompt/response content. If Acme requires that even metadata remain exclusively in-region, we can offer an Enterprise Private deployment (VPC/private control plane) or a contractual amendment limiting what is shared.

3) Subprocessors & access:
- Our current subprocessors list is on the link below; for EU accounts the primary subprocessors that handle data are: EU object storage (managed provider in eu-west-1), monitoring provider (EU tenancy where available), and select support tools. Some vendors operate globally but have EU-only tenancy options.
- We do not grant access to raw customer content to engineering vendors outside the EU unless explicit access is required for troubleshooting and is approved under an ACL and documented change.

4) Contractual options & DPA amendments:
- We can: (a) add explicit DPA language that states backups and snapshots will remain in the EU and that Redwood will not enable cross-region replication without written consent; or (b) provide a Private deployment with a customer-managed control plane to eliminate control-plane metadata transfer to the US.
- For high-assurance needs (legal requirement to avoid any US jurisdiction exposure), Private deployment is the recommended path. For most customers, a DPA amendment combined with logging/data minimization controls is sufficient.

5) Next steps / artifacts I've attached:
- redwood_dpa_eu_excerpt.pdf (standard DPA language for EU accounts)
- Link to subprocessors page: https://redwood.example.com/subprocessors
- We'll also provide SOC 2 cover letters and the specific controls mapping if you want them.

If you'd like, we can draft proposed DPA wording (sample clause included below) and route it to Acme legal. We can also schedule a short technical call with our infra team to walk through where specific logs live.

Sample clause (for discussion):
"Redwood shall not enable cross-region replication of customer primary storage, backups or snapshots for accounts pinned to the EU region without Customer's prior written consent. Control-plane operational telemetry shall be minimised to account identifiers and aggregated usage metrics; no customer prompt/response content will be stored or processed in the US control plane."

Happy to iterate — let me know which path you prefer and we'll prepare the DPA amendment or Private deployment options and a targeted architecture session.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
